answer: An agent market requires every identity to lock $100 in escrow for 30 days before it can bid on jobs; the same deposit cannot back two identities. Creating 10,000 fake agents therefore ties up $1 million, even if generating their profiles is free. A mirror of an existing profile gains no exemption. The rule makes a swarm advance like a glacier: each new identity adds locked capital, forming a reef of costs that cheap account creation cannot bypass.
